decisions.rationale: Current e-Gov 労働安全衛生規則第34条の2の5第1項 expressly requires the Article 57-2(1) notification to be made by the time the notified substance is transferred or provided, subject to the stated repeated-transfer exception when notification has already been made. The stem asks the ordinary statutory timing rule and D reproduces that rule without adding an unsupported pre-notice or post-transfer deadline. A, B, C and E are plausible timing misconceptions but are not the statutory rule. No current canonical or persisted Eisei1 item tests SDS/notification timing.

Current e-Gov 鉛中毒予防規則第53条第1項 requires the periodic lead medical examination generally every six months, while the paragraph's parenthetical specifies every one year for the listed lead-work categories and cleaning work at those workplaces. B correctly states that general/exception structure. C reverses it; D invents a two-year rule and also ignores the separate, condition-heavy one-year relaxation provision; A and E are inconsistent with Article 53. The proposition is distinct from the canonical ionizing-radiation examination interval and from specified-chemical/asbestos record questions.

Current e-Gov 粉じん障害防止規則第22条第1項 lists exactly five special-education subjects for workers regularly assigned to specified dust work: dust-emission prevention and workplace ventilation methods, workplace management, respiratory-protective-equipment use, dust-related disease and health management, and relevant laws. A is the only choice that matches all five subjects. The distractors substitute related but non-listed topics. This legal education-content proposition is materially distinct from B8's hygiene-lane question about equipment and wetting measures applied to a specific dust emission source.
